subject: Order form — exposure metric harmonization & annual reset options
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Legal <sara.legal@acme-analytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — exposure basis for liability cap

Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the draft MSA + order form and procurement is flagging a couple of items that will block our PO unless we reach alignment on exposure and bake in an annual reconciliation. High level:

- We cannot accept a single contract lifetime cap tied to total historical fees for multi-year deals; procurement prefers an annualized approach that resets each 12‑month billing period.
- If you insist on a cumulative cap, we need a clear floor/ceiling formula (e.g., capped at 2x annual fees, or $2M, whichever is lower).
- We want consequential damages excluded but with carve-outs for IP infringement and gross negligence.

Can you share the options you can live with (simple redline or bullets work), and whether Redwood can include an annual reconciliation clause? We aim to finalize order form and issue a PO by end of month.

Thanks — copying Sara (legal) and Laura from your side.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: Order form — exposure basis for liability cap

Daniel — thanks for the clear note. Appreciate the timeline. I sketched three pragmatic approaches below (attached a short slide with worked examples: redwood-cap-examples.pdf).

Option 1 — Per-contract aggregate cap
- Single aggregate liability cap equal to the aggregate fees paid under the specific order form (1x fees paid)
- No annual reset; simple to administer for us but not aligned with your ask

Option 2 — Annualized cap with reset (recommended)
- Cap = 2x fees invoiced during each 12‑month period (annual reset at anniversary of first invoice)
- Aggregate exposure limited per year; for multi‑year deals total exposure will therefore be a multiple of annual fees but resets each year
- Consequential damages excluded except for IP infringement and gross negligence; regulatory fines remain carve‑out subject to insurer confirmation

Option 3 — Hybrid floors & ceilings
- Per incident cap $750k; annual aggregate 3x annual fees (whichever is lower)
- Useful if you want per‑incident predictability and an annual safety valve

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Option 2 gives Acme the annual reset you asked for and aligns with our underwriting models.
- We can add narrow carve‑outs: IP indemnity, willful misconduct, and third‑party claims tied to customer data misuse.
- If you require regulatory fines as a carve‑out, that will likely require us to talk to our insurers; can be done but may change commercial terms.

Next steps: I can set up a 30‑minute call between Laura, Karthik, your counsel (Sara) and me to pick one option and agree redline language. If you want us to produce a marked MSA + order form with your preferred option, we can do that within 2 business days after the call.

Attaching: redwood-cap-examples.pdf (simple numbers + plain‑English redline snippets)

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Order form — exposure basis for liability cap

Vivek / team — quick legal view before the call. I reviewed Vivek's options and drafted a focused redline (attached: redwood-msa-redline.docx). My recommended negotiation posture: pursue Option 2 (annualized cap with reset) with the following guardrails: 

1) Cap calculation
- Language: "Customer's liability for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to two times (2x) the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood for the services rendered in the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the claim."

2) Carve-outs (narrow):
- IP indemnity (full carve‑out)
- Gross negligence and willful misconduct (not subject to cap)
- Third‑party claims arising from Redwood's breach of confidentiality obligations (not subject to cap)

3) Consequential damages
- Keep standard exclusion for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, but explicitly preserve claims for statutory or regulatory penalties only where required by law (we should avoid broadly carving regulatory fines unless we get insurer signoff).

4) Practical language for annual reset
- Add a single sentence tying the reset to the anniversary of the first invoice and requiring mutual reconciliation if invoices are prorated across a shortened first period.

5) Commercial fallback
- If Acme insists on regulatory fines carve‑out, recommend we reserve right to reprice (discount reduction or additional cap uplift).

I'll be on the call to run legal through redline language. Markus — FYI on insurer conversation if client pushes regulatory fines.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Vivek / Laura — thanks, that layout helps. Acme's position: we prefer Option 2 with the annual reset and the 2x annual fees formula, subject to the narrow carve‑outs you list (IP + gross negligence + confidentiality). Two clarifications before we lock: 

1) Please confirm whether Redwood will accept "regulatory fines" as an exception to the cap. If you need to consult insurers, let us know timing — we would prefer a definitive answer before issuing PO.
2) For the annual reset, please add a short example in the order form showing how the first partial year is annualized (simple prorate is fine).

If you can confirm those two items and provide the marked MSA + order form redline, we can proceed to PO. Proposed call: Thu 14 Oct 10:00am PT if that works for legal.

Best,
—Daniel
